assets.title: Concrete 048
assets.author: ambientCG
assets.authorNote: ambientCG is the credited source brand; official imprint names operator Lennart Demes. Asset pages do not name an additional individual author.
assets.role: Clean industrial concrete or subtle floor microtexture. Keep raised-floor seams authored by existing scene geometry.

realistic.note: Six maps, keep existing palette as constant base colors. Add Metal032 Color only if its cool satin-grey hue is desired. Avoid using the beige Concrete048 Color for the entire datacenter. Normal scales start at 0.15 metal, 0.12 powdercoat, 0.10 floor; tune at final camera distance.

simple.note: Three roughness maps only. Preserve the current clean silhouette and palette; optional Metal032 NormalGL at normalScale 0.04 if a close view needs it. Use constant metalness values instead of separate metalness textures.

notes: Color map uses SRGBColorSpace. Roughness and NormalGL are non-color data; leave NoColorSpace.
NormalGL is OpenGL tangent-space. Do not use NormalDX or invert the green channel when using these NormalGL files.
Repeat texture tiles at believable small surface scale. Share texture objects/materials across repeated racks. Do not allocate unique maps per rack.
No displacement, AO, metalness maps, USD, Blender, or preview images needed in the site build. The original zip archives are research provenance only.
Painted black powdercoat is primarily a dielectric topcoat: start metalness at 0.05. Bare Metal032 may start at 0.8. These are proposed visual settings, not measured material values.
Roughness maps multiply the material roughness scalar in Three. Check highlights at actual scene lighting; keep floor rougher than metal.
Use restrained normalScale, with no geometric displacement. Existing mesh seams and ventilation details should remain legible.
